name: Zimbabwe Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress
sweep_summary: Zimbabwe Sign Language (zimb1247) is not in the catalog and, as a sign language, has no spoken-language word stress to code. Both title-keyword hits in the list of works with stress in the title are Glottolog noise: their records carry language code = {Zimbabwe Sign Language [zib] (computerized assignment from "academic")}, i.e. the word 'academic' in the titles triggered the tag. Renk & Smith 2007 is a psychology paper on academic stress in US college students; Ho 2016 is an Appraisal-theory discourse analysis of Hong Kong quality-check reports ('evaluative prosodies' = semantic prosody). Neither mentions Zimbabwe, sign language, or linguistic stress. Nothing to acquire (priority none). The pre-existing check in (Glottolog page, ISO/SIL records, four open-access ZSL papers by Matende & Hlungwani 2025, Matende et al. 2024, Ndlovu & Makwavarara 2023) already found no source stating anything about stress or prosody in ZSL; the only ZSL paper using 'prosodic' (Matende & Hlungwani 2025, Negation) does so in citing non-manual-prosody work on Israeli, German and American Sign Language, not ZSL. Records downloaded this search of works with stress in the title (Glottolog refs 440694 and 549439, two Crossref JSONs) are saved there and logged in under 'search of works with stress or accent in the title '. no best new statement found.
